text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish construction firm Exbud SA, which despite increasing demand will face growing domestic and foreign competition, Bank Handlowy said in a report.

"At a price of 39.6 zlotys per share, we recommend holding shares of Exbud. At this price, the level of the p/e ratio for 1996 amounts to about 34.7...At the end of 1997, according to our forecasts, its level will fall to 28.3," the report said.
The report was dated February 14 and released to the press on Monday, when preliminary results show Exbud shares closing at 40.7 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse's main market.
Handlowy said a good sign was Exbud's limiting of its activities outside construction, but that the current structure of its group was unclear and discouraging some investors.
It said Exbud would likely maintain its leading position on the domestic market but that exports of construction services to both Western and Eastern Europe were seen dropping.
Handlowy sees Exbud lifting net profits this year to 14 million zlotys from 11.4 million in 1996. It said sales would rise to 400 million zlotys from 311.2 million in 1996.
